title: A sensor that runs on the machine it watches
intro: Industrial machines vibrate all day. This cantilever turns that wasted motion into electricity for a wireless sensor that reports faults before they become breakdowns.
credit: Our group's chosen design, picked with a weighted decision matrix over four concepts. Concept led by my teammate Chiedozie Obodoechi; I co-led the research and the technical overview with him.
facts: IY1EH5 Engineering Global Challenge, University of Hull

parts.name: Base mass
parts.text: Bonded to the machine with epoxy. Stiff enough to pass every vibration straight into the beam, and a mount for the PCB.

parts.name: Cantilever beam
parts.text: Bends with each vibration and carries the PZT layer. Stainless for its stiffness and steady behaviour under cyclic bending.

parts.name: PZT layer
parts.text: Turns bending stress into voltage. It stops short of the tip because the stress is highest at the root.

parts.name: Electrodes
parts.text: Thin silver films on both faces of the PZT collect the charge without stiffening the beam.

parts.name: Proof mass
parts.text: Adds inertia at the free end to bend the beam further and pull its resonance down to 30 to 35 Hz machinery.

parts.name: Wires
parts.text: Soldered to the electrodes, strain-relieved with epoxy and twisted to reject noise on the way to the PCB.

how.title: How it works
items: Vibrate
The machine shakes the base; the beam and proof mass swing hardest when the machine's frequency matches the beam's resonance.
Convert
Bending stresses the PZT layer, which produces an alternating voltage. A four-diode bridge rectifies it into a storage capacitor.
Store and send
At 2.2 V a relay connects the sensor network: accelerometer, microcontroller and sub-GHz radio. It runs until the capacitor falls to 1.6 V.
Retune
Below 1.6 V, a variable load shifts the harvester's resonance towards the machine's, keeping power up when the vibration changes.

did.title: What we did
items: Chose the concept
Scored four concepts in a weighted decision matrix and picked the piezo harvester.
CAD
Modelled the base, cantilever, PZT layer, proof mass and wiring in SolidWorks.
Circuit
Built a Simulink model of the rectifier, storage capacitor and relay-switched tuning.
Tuning
Used MATLAB to choose the proof mass for 30 to 35 Hz machinery and find the best load resistance.
Power budget
Checked the duty cycle of sleeping, sensing and transmitting against the harvested power.
Build and risks
Wrote the build procedure, a risk assessment and a bill of materials of about £15.

improve.title: What we'd improve
items: Effective mass
The model puts the whole beam's mass at the tip. Using its effective mass, about a quarter, moves 5.7 g from 29.8 Hz to about 32.6 Hz, inside the band.
Prototype
Build one and measure it on a shaker table to check the real resonance and output.
PCB
Model the PCB and enclosure, which the CAD leaves out.
Harvesting IC
Swap the discrete tuning circuit for a dedicated piezo harvesting chip such as the LTC3588.
Fatigue
Check the stainless beam's fatigue life at full resonant amplitude.
Wider band
Add a second beam or magnetic tuning so one unit covers more machine speeds.
